item.title: 55 years ago the Dallas Cowboys opened this Super Bowl-winning stadium
item.description: General view of the interior of Texas Stadium during the game between the Washington Redskins and the Dallas Cowboys on September 28, 2008 at Texas Stadium in Irving, Texas. (Tim Umphrey/Getty Images) Dallas Cowboys fans are either celebrating another win or recovering from another loss on Thanksgiving (we don't know at the time of writing). There once was a time when Cowboys fans had almost a guarantee of success on Thanksgiving Day, but those odds seem less and less likely every year. We've already looked at the Cowboys' 30 worst moments in the 30 years since their last Super Bowl , but let's propose that the Cowboys' string of bad luck might be because they demolished their good luck charm. It has now been 55 years since Texas Stadium opened in Irving. The venue debuted in 1971 as the new home of the Dallas Cowboys, who previously played at the Cotton Bowl, and was famous for its hole in the roof that linebacker D.D. Lewis said was "so God can watch His favorite team play." Regardless, the Cowboys had their greatest successes at Texas Stadium, winning all five of the franchise's Super Bowls, including Super Bowl VI the same season Texas Stadium opened. The stadium was demolished in 2010 after the Cowboys moved into AT&T Stadium and the wins have paled in comparison. Coincidence? Let's look at the numbers. Head coach Tom Landry of the Dallas Cowboys stands with his team before coming onto the field before an NFL football game circa 1978 at Texas Stadium in Dallas, Texas. (Focus On Sport/Getty Images) Rear view of Dallas Cowboys QB Troy Aikman (8) in action, passing vs Phoenix Cardinals at Texas Stadium. (Al Tielemans/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images) From 1971 through 2008, the Cowboys went 346-240, winning 59% of their games. Since then, it's been a slight drop, going 153-123-1 and winning 55% of games. However, the real impact is seen in the postseason. At Texas Stadium, the Cowboys appeared in 13 NFC Championship Games, played in seven Super Bowls, and won five. Since moving to AT&T Stadium in 2009, the Cowboys have made seven playoff appearances, won four playoff games and have yet to make an appearance in the NFC Championship. So, yes, Cowboys fans can point to many things for their struggles. The departure of Jimmy Johnson, the failures of Barry Switzer, poor choices in the draft, bad free agent signings or countless referee errors. But perhaps it's none of that. Texas Stadium was demolished on April 11, 2010. Perhaps the football gods have not looked kindly on the boys in blue ever since; punishment for choosing the billion-dollar arena over the legacy built in Irving. Ironically, the Cowboys have won four straight games on Thanksgiving heading into this week. So, maybe that's a consolation prize. Victories on Thanksgiving in exchange for heartbreak in winter. item.title: Every player from California to play for the Brooklyn Nets - David Nwaba
item.description: The Brooklyn Nets have signed, drafted, and traded for players from virtually every state in the US, and much of the wider world beyond the United States. From Alabama to Wyoming, and from Australia to Ukraine, the Nets have a long and distinguished history of turning over every stone to find the talent needed to succeed in the NBA. From their start in the American Basketball Association (ABA) as the New Jersey Americans and New York Nets to their jump to the NBA as the New Jersey Nets right through to today, the organization has cast their net for talent wide since the inception of the ball club. For this installment of our series documenting the provenience of every Nets player to suit up for the franchise, let's take a look at every player from California who has played for Brooklyn. Our focus in this article is David Nwaba. An alum of Cal Poly, he went unselected in the 2016 NBA Draft, playing in other leagues until he signed with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2017. The Los Angeles, California native played the first season of his pro career with Los Angeles. He also played for the Chicago Bulls and Cleveland Cavaliers before he signed with the Brooklyn Nets in 2019. His stay with the team lasted until he was cut in 2020. During his time suiting up for the Nets, Nwaba put up 5.2 points and 2.3 rebounds per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. item.title: What happened the last time Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner did not compete at a Grand Slam event
item.description: Jannik Sinner is set to miss the 2026 Australian Open due to injury. The Italian superstar suffered a debilitating knee injury in the lead-up to the US Open and has been absent from the Tour ever since. Sinner underwent knee surgery earlier this week and is now set to spend significantly more time on the sidelines. “We’ve been in regular touch with Jannik’s team and they’ve confirmed he won’t be joining us for the Australian Open in January following his recent surgery,” Tennis Australia chief Andrew Abdo said in a statement to AFP on Thursday. Tennis fans are now set to witness four consecutive Grand Slam events without the presence of both Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner . The last time Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner did not both compete in a Grand Slam singles event You have to go back seven years to locate the last instance in which Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner did not compete in a single major event. Neither player qualified for the 2019 Wimbledon Championships . Sinner was knocked out in the first round of qualifying by Alex Bolt, and Alcaraz did not make his ATP Tour debut until February 2020 at the Rio Open. At the 2019 Championships, Novak Djokovic and Roger Federer advanced to the men’s singles final in south-west London. Djokovic defeated David Goffin and Roberto Bautista Agut en route to the final, while Federer overcame the likes of Kei Nishikori and Rafael Nadal. What ensued was one of the greatest Grand Slam finals in tennis history. At 7-6, 1-6, 7-6, 4-6, 7-8, Federer led 40-15 and held two championship points on his serve. Djokovic produced some sublime tennis to deny Federer, and eventually won the final set 13-12. Djokovic became the first man since Bob Falkenburg in 1948 to win Wimbledon after being championship points down. “It’s quite unreal,” Djokovic said afterwards. Photo by BEN STANSALL/AFP via Getty Images “Like similar to ’08 maybe, I will look back at it and think, ‘well, it’s not that bad after all’. For now it hurts, and it should, like every loss does here at Wimbledon,” Federer said. “Epic ending, so close, so many moments. Yeah, I mean, sure there’s similarities [between this and his 2008 Wimbledon final loss to Rafael Nadal]. I’m the loser both times, so that’s the only similarity I see.” How did Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner perform in their first Grand Slam events? Alcaraz qualified for his first main draw at a Grand Slam at the 2021 Australian Open. The Spaniard triumphed on his debut, beating Botic van de Zandschulp 6-1, 6-4, 6-4. He was then beaten by Mikael Ymer in four sets. Sinner made his debut 18 months earlier, at the 2019 US Open. The Italian failed to win on debut, losing to Stan Wawrinka in four sets. Sinner secured his first Grand Slam win at the 2020 Australian Open after defeating Max Purcell in straight sets. Marton Fucsovics ended Sinner’s run in the second round, winning 6-4, 6-4, 6-3.

item.title: Meet the ‘Bash Brothers’ of the Utah Mammoth
item.description: Utah Mammoth center Jack McBain (22) and Colorado Avalanche left wing Gabriel Landeskog (92) fight during an NHL game at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. | Scott G Winterton, Deseret News Remember the “Bash Brothers” from the second “Mighty Ducks” movie? That’s a thing in the NHL now. OK, nobody in the NHL — or the real world in general — will ever get away with all the blatant interference that Fulton Reed and Dean Portman did in the movie. But Utah Mammoth forwards Jack McBain and Liam O’Brien, who co-lead the league in fighting majors this season, are developing that reputation. View this post on Instagram Anyone who pays close attention to the Mammoth is familiar with the rough-and-tumble personalities of McBain and “Spicy Tuna.” To them, sleeves are optional and facial hair is not. After their interview with the TNT panel after a fiery game against the Colorado Avalanche on Nov. 18, the hockey world got a proper introduction to the swinging fists of the Mammoth. Panelist Paul “Biznasty” Bissonnette, who, according to HockeyFights.com, amassed 200 fights over his 16 years playing junior and pro hockey, even bestowed the “Bash Brothers” nickname upon them. “The NHL is different today than it was even 10 years ago, 20 years ago. I think people sometimes don’t realize that.” Liam O’Brien, Utah Mammoth After some fights tonight, Jack McBain AND Liam O'Brien joined the boys postgame 🥊🔥 Also Biz struck out again asking player to flex... again 😂 pic.twitter.com/Mv1xAzAPCF — NHLonTNT (@NHL_On_TNT) November 19, 2026 Few, if any, NHL tough guys grow up dreaming of filling the role of a fighter. At least in the modern era, they all grew up as skilled players — physicality is just something a player would add to his résumé to both get noticed and provide more value to his team. “As you get older, you’ve got to learn how you can be effective and learn different parts of the game,” McBain said in the TNT interview. “I’m a big guy. I like to play physical, and sometimes that style of hockey makes you have to answer the bell.” O’Brien came just short of a point per game at the U18 AAA level. He flashed a bit of that skill against the Avalanche, scoring on a one-timer and hitting a pair of posts thereafter. He’s known for his physicality, but he came a few inches away from scoring a hat trick in the NHL. When asked whether it feels like people don’t recognize that skill, O’Brien gave an insightful answer. “Yeah, I mean, the NHL is different today than it was even 10 years ago, 20 years ago,” he told the Deseret News. “I think people sometimes don’t realize that. But yeah, that’s fine. “I really don’t care what anybody thinks, to be honest. I know my game. I know my teammates know my game. I know my coaches and my management know my game. So people can say I’m a fighter, enforcer or whatever. It just doesn’t matter. It doesn’t matter to me. The only thing that matters is what I am for this team, and that’s just what I focus on.”

item.description: Cowboys playoff picture: Updated chances for Dallas to make 2026 NFL postseason in Week 12 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Cowboys haven't made the NFC Championship Game in 31 years. In the 2026 NFL regular season, they're just trying to return to the NFC playoffs for the first time in three years. There are low expectations for the Cowboys to make the postseason. They have struggled to get to .500 and stay above it this season. They blew a big chance to even their record by blowing a 31-10 lead in a 39-38 upset loss to the Eagles in Thursday's Week 12 division matchup. With six weeks left, here's breaking down Dallas' updated chances of making the field as NFC East champion or a wild-card team: MORE: Updated NFL playoff picture for Week 12 Cowboys playoff picture The Cowboys (5-7) are down to third place in the NFC East, two-and-a-half games behind the Giants (6-3-1). They are a half-game behind the third-place Commanders (4-5-1). In the big picture of the NFC standings, the Cowboys are No. 11, two-and-a-half games behind the Rams (7-4), who hold the final wild-card position at No. 7. The Seahawks (6-4), Packers (6-5) and Commanders are all between the Rams and Cowboys. Cowboys remaining schedule Week 13: at Seahawks Week 14: bye Week 15: at Rams Week 16: vs. Jaguars Week 17: vs. Giants Week 18: at Commanders The Cowboys, per Tankathon , have a remaining schedule strength of No. 2 in the NFL, as their final five opponents have a combined current winning percentage of .605. The only opponent left with a losing record is Washington. The Seahawks are the most difficult road game. The Jaguars are the most difficult home game. Looking at that gauntlet, finishing 3-2 will keep the Cowboys under .500 at 8-9. The best-case scenario is finishing 9-8 and hoping that's enough to win the division. Dallas' defensive struggles will keep it from going better than 4-1. Cowboys' playoff chances The Cowboys would finish 4-2 in division play if they win the remaining rematches with the Giants and Commanders. Losing the Packers tiebreaker is tough. The Cowboys also cannot afford to lose to both the Rams and Seahawks, and just losing to either can be bad enough. That would make the wild-card path impossible to clear. Then it would be hoping that 9-8 is can still win a weak division. The Giants would then need to finish 2-5 for the Cowboys to win the division. The Cowboys' playoff chances stood at about 15 percent going into Week 12, and they would have improved to only 20 percent with a win over the Eagles. But the shocking loss in their most winnable game puts their chances of making the NFC playoffs at less than 10 percent. MORE: Why Cowboys always play on Thanksgiving

item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 26: Jeremy Fears Jr. #1 and Kur Teng #2 of the Michigan State Spartans celebrate following a made three point basket basket from Teng during the second half against the Arkansas Razorbacks in the CBS Thanksgiving Classic at Little Caesars Arena on November 26, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Jaime Crawford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Michigan State Spartans and the Arkansas Razorbacks gave the fans a highly entertaining back-and-forth game on Thanksgiving. I will get to the game in a minute, but first I am going to talk a bit about something that Tom Izzo mentioned at the beginning of his post-game press conference, and that is the Detroit Lions game. Fortunately for me, I live about five minutes from Little Caesars arena so I was able to watch the entirety of the Lions game before darting over for the MSU game. I only missed the first five minutes of the action at LCA. But the end of that Lions game ruined my entire day. item.description: Australian fielder Cameron Bancroft (R) is questioned by the umpires after using sandpaper in the third Test against South Africa in 2018 (GIANLUIGI GUERCIA) Cricket Australia widened its independent "Sandpapergate" forum on Friday to include the preceding Ashes series against England, while pledging to make the findings and its response public. The governing body has ruled out reopening its investigation into the explosive 2018 ball-tampering scandal in South Africa that blew up again this month. Instead, it proposed a forum for players, coaches and staff on the tour to share their versions of events. In a surprise development, the terms of reference released Friday broadened to include "ball-management practices" during the 2017-2018 season, including the home Ashes series which Australia won 4-0. The hosts' consistent ability to get reverse swing in that series had England's bowlers scratching their heads. In the wake of the South Africa fallout, England great Alastair Cook, who was part of the Ashes side, was asked whether the team suspected Australia of ball-tampering. "Yes a little bit, certainly in Perth when the outfield was wet with rain they got the ball-reversing," he said. The issue went no further. Experienced senior counsel Fiona McLeod will lead the forum, which will be open for six weeks and is voluntary. Players' accounts, which can be written or verbal, will be confidential. She will investigate the Ashes, all four Tests of the South Africa tour, the events of March 24, 2018, when Cameron Bancroft was caught with sandpaper, and the conduct of the 2018 Cricket Australia probe. McLeod will provide a report detailing the principal themes and her recommendations. But what players say will not be published, no new sanctions will come out of it and she is not charged with determining any individual responsibility. "This is an opportunity to provide their accounts in a safe environment and to provide the CA board with relevant information including about the events of that tour and resultant investigation," said Cricket Australia interim chairman David Boon. "We are acutely aware of the enormous toll the renewed focus on this tour eight years ago has had on those involved and their welfare remains our main priority. "This forum is the best opportunity for people to speak and be heard, and for CA to listen and learn," added Boon. "Publishing the report in full is part of our commitment to transparency, and to be open with cricket fans about what we learn. Somehow, some way, the Cowboys threw away a 31-10 lead that they had in the third quarter. The Philadelphia Eagles won on what was basically a game-winning, 60-yard field goal. It is hard to fathom. On the other hand it is actually very easy to fathom given everything we have seen from the Cowboys this season. They are not a good football team. They are poorly coached. They are talent-deficient.
